text:
Alex M.: Hey team — customer (Helena) reports repeated 429s during short bursts, even though they think they have headroom on both org and project quotas. They see mixed behavior: some requests return 429 with X-RateLimit-Scope: org, others 429 with X-RateLimit-Id: project, and once a 401 when rotating keys. Link to logs they pasted below.
Helena (customer): Logged around 2026-02-28T15:04Z. We have org id `org_9ab3`, project `proj-ghost`, and a set of two API keys; traffic goes through a corporate NATed proxy (single egress IP). The app spikes (30 reqs/s for ~20s) every minute. After a spike we see a sustained 429 window for ~2 minutes.
Alex M.: Snippet of headers they captured:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1670000000
X-RateLimit-Scope: org
X-RateLimit-Id: org_9ab3
Retry-After: 120
```

and another sample from same minute:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1670000000
X-RateLimit-Scope: project
X-RateLimit-Id: proj-ghost
Retry-After: 30
```

Helena (customer): Also saw a `401` once after key rotation, but that might be a separate auth TTL issue.
Priya S.: Is the proxy reusing the same API key across customers or doing header rewriting? If the proxy is pooling requests from multiple internal services under one egress IP, IP-based caps could be colliding with org/project keys.
Helena (customer): Proxy doesn't touch the Authorization header. It does NAT. Multiple projects from same org share the egress IP.
Alex M.: Quick notes on our rate-limit logic that matter here:
- We apply tokens at multiple scopes: API-key (per-key), project, org, and IP. Enforcement falls back to the most-constraining scope at the moment of evaluation.
- Burst window behavior: an internal token-bucket allows ephemeral bursts (burst_seconds ~ 10s) but only if token buckets at all scopes have spare tokens at check time.
- When multiple requests arrive simultaneously from same IP but different keys, IP scoping can trigger a single aggregated throttle which appears as org/project 429s depending on which check fails first.
Samir (eng-runtime): From logs I see two weird things: (1) quota counters updated asynchronously — there is a short delay (200-500ms) between a heavy burst and the project/org counters being updated in the central store; (2) the proxy's single IP is exceeding the IP-per-minute threshold so IP-based enforcement is firing often, and we map that back to the org when the token check for org is evaluated before project.
Alex M.: Helena, can you reproduce with a simple script we can run here? Priya suggests a small curl loop that mimics their spike so we can correlate our server-side traces.
Helena (customer): Yes, happy to. What should I run?
Alex M.: Please run this from the same machine behind your proxy (so same egress IP):

```
# from customer host
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY1>" -H "X-Project-ID: proj-ghost" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" &
  sleep 0.03
done
wait
```

And then re-run swapping `<KEY1>` to `<KEY2>` and one run with both keys interleaved. Capture response codes and any `Retry-After` headers.
Helena (customer): Ran the 200-loop with KEY1: got ~140 200s then a burst of 429s, Retry-After mostly 120. With KEY2 alone similar. With both interleaved we saw earlier 429s and Retry-After 30 on some responses.
Priya S.: That pattern suggests the project bucket and IP bucket have different windows and limits. When single key spikes, project-level throttle is the limiting factor (longer reset). When two keys interleave, the IP or per-key bucket may get depleted faster causing shorter reset window 30s.
Samir (eng-runtime): I pulled the trace for org_9ab3 at the time range. We have these counts in the metric store (windowed): org tokens consumed: 1800 in 1m, project tokens consumed: 320 in 1m, ip tokens consumed: 2400 in 1m. Our enforcement checks order: api-key -> project -> org -> ip (configurable). If project check failed it returns project 429; if org failed before project due to asynchronous updates you can get org 429s.
Jordan (eng-infra): Two immediate suspects: (A) the NATed IP pushes the IP bucket over fast and our mapping to org/project is ambiguous when multiple keys share the IP; (B) counter propagation lag: the central quota store sharded updates and uses eventual consistency for throughput, which can cause order-of-check races under heavy bursts.
Alex M.: Actionable steps:
- Short-term workaround for customer: use per-key rate limiting isolation (we can enable "strict per-key" mode for their org) which forces us to evaluate and enforce per-key quotas before aggregating by IP/org. This reduces cross-project interference but may reduce overall throughput.
- Medium-term: we can increase the project burst window for proj-ghost by 2x or bump project/minute quota if their contract allows.
- Long-term: eng-infra to make enforcement checks read consistent snapshot (or add leader read) for sequential burst path or tweak propagation TTL to <100ms for quota counters.
Samir (eng-runtime): Quick config snippet I can toggle for Helena's org so you can test right away:

```
# patch to rate-limit policy
PATCH /internal/policies/org_9ab3
{
  "enforce_order": ["api-key","project","org","ip"],
  "per_key_isolation": true,
  "burst_seconds_override": 20
}
```

Alex M.: Samir — does enabling per_key_isolation have a risk of bypassing IP limits entirely? Helena's proxy would still face IP limits if we keep IP enforcement, right?
Samir (eng-runtime): Correct — IP enforcement still runs, but per_key_isolation makes us fail earlier on per-key exhaustion rather than attributing it to a shared org or IP bucket. That often gives nicer Retry-After semantics for multi-tenant proxies. We won't disable IP enforcement unless requested.
Helena (customer): Would enabling per_key_isolation stop the 401 after key rotation? That one was scary.
Priya S.: 401 is separate. Could be a short TTL for the signing key cache in our auth layer. We saw a bug last month where key rotation could surface a 401 within 10s for some edge paths; eng-infra had a patch but might not be rolled to all regions.
Jordan (eng-infra): I will check rollout status and confirm. If still present we'll push the hotfix to the control plane in region eu-west-1.
Alex M.: Repro guidance for us: Helena please paste a small sample of the `curl -v` output showing headers where you got a 401 and the two different 429 types. We'll attach traces (X-Trace-Id) from those responses.
Helena (customer): Pasted: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` with body `{"error":"invalid_api_key"}` and header `X-Trace-Id: trace-9f3b` from 2026-02-28T15:05:12Z. Also two 429s: `X-Trace-Id: trace-a12` and `trace-b34`.
Samir (eng-runtime): Got the trace ids. I see that `trace-9f3b` hits auth cache miss and the auth backend returned 200 on re-check within 3s. Likely the rotation race. We'll add a small grace window for rotated keys for 60s.
Alex M.: Tentative plan and owners:
- Enable per_key_isolation for org_9ab3 (Samir) — test with Helena (high priority, expected <1h to toggle + monitor).
- Check auth cache key rotation hotfix rollout (Jordan) — confirm within 2h.
- If per_key_isolation doesn't fully resolve, bump project quota / burst window (Priya) — coordinate with sales/CS for quota change.
- Engineering follow-up: eng-infra to evaluate consistency of quota counters and consider leader-read or decreasing propagation TTL (Jordan + Samir) — triage in next sprint.
Helena (customer): Thanks all. We'll test per_key_isolation now.
RateLimitBot: Incident note created: INC-2026-4423 — "org_9ab3 burst-induced mixed-scope 429s". Assigned to Samir, Jordan.
Alex M.: Marking this resolved for support once Helena confirms per-key toggle. Keep this thread for notes.
Helena (customer): After per_key_isolation enabled: observed fewer cross-key 429s, most 429s now have X-RateLimit-Id: api_key and Retry-After = 30s. The 401 hasn't reappeared in 12m. Thank you!
Alex M.: Great. Closing support escalation. If you want, we can open a formal eng bug for counter consistency and follow up in eng-runtime. :tada:
